HIGH COURT RULES
HIGH COURT RULES
AND ORDERS
(VOL. IV)
CHAPTER 12
OATHS, AFFIRMATIONS AND
AFFIDAVITS
PART A
1. Oaths and affirmations: In the exercise of the
power conferred by Section 7 of the Oaths Act, 1873, the High Court hereby
prescribes the following form for oaths and affirmations, to be made by
witnesses, who may be required to give evidence by or before any Court or duly
authorised person, and by interpreters.
(Words Omitted vide C.P.
No.53 & CS No.137 dated 10-8-1987.)
Appropriate form: (1) The first column in each table
indicates what is the appropriate form for the persons there described.
2. Suitable forms to meet
different cases: One or other of the form prescribed is suitable for
administration to any person who is competent to testify or to interpret, [ ]. The forms have been adapted to meet
all objections which can be raised by a Court or by a person required to give
evidence, to interpret or to act as a Juror; to administering or to making (as
the case may be) an oath or a solemn affirmation on the ground of immature age,
want of or defect in religious belief, or any similar ground, in respect of the
person to be affirmed or sworn.
(Words Omitted vide C.P.
No.53 & CS No.137 dated 10-8-1987.)
3. Oaths under Section 8 of the Oaths Act not
affected: The oath and
solemn affirmations referred to in Section 8 of the Oaths Act, 1873, are not in
any way effected by these instructions.
4. Change in form when witness is not a
resident of Pakistan: [Omitted vide 9.P. No.53 & C S No.137, dated 10-8-1987.]
5. Manner of administering oath: Before a witness is called on to
give evidence he should be made to stand in front of the Presiding Officer who
will himself administer the oath or affirmation to him solemnly and
impressively, making the witness respect the words in a clear voice, phrase for
phrase. While the oath or affirmation is thus being administered everyone in
Court shall be made to stand in complete allence.
2. Oaths taken on Guru Granth Sahib: If in any case oath is to be taken
on Guru Granth Sahib, it should be taken in Gurdawara with the permission and
in the person of the Granthi or an authorised representative of the Gurdawara
Committee, as the case may be, Guru Granth Sahib should in no case be brought
into Court for this purpose.
3. When oath or affirmation may be dispensed
with: Attention is
drawn to Federal Government Act, 39 of 1939 amending the Oaths Act, 1973. This
Act lays down that when a witness is under 12 years of age and the Court has reason
to believe, that though he understands the duty of speaking the truth he does
not understand the nature of an oath or affirmation, he shall not be asked to
make an oath or affirmation; but in any such case the absence of an oath or
affirmation shall not render inadmissible any evidence given by such witness
nor effect the obligation of the witness to state the truth.

WITNESSES.

Form of oath or affirmation to be
administered to witness in civil and criminal cases or in a proceeding before
any other authority empowered to administer an oath or affirmation and to
take evidence.
(A) Simple Affirmation:
For a person who has an
objection to making an oath or solemn affirmation, or who, by reason of
immature age, or of the want of or defect in religious belief, ought no, in
the opinion of the Court or person authorized to administer an oath or
affirmation, to be permitted to take an oath or solemn affirmations.
I solemnly affirm that the evidence which I shall give to the Court,
or as the case may be, in this case (or matter) shall be the truth, the whole
truth, and nothing but the truth.

For a non-Muslim, who
has an objection to making oath.
